title: Recall Quiz: Early Victorians: Tennyson, Browning, Brontës

questions.q: A poem in which a single fictional character speaks to a silent listener, inadvertently revealing their own psychological flaws, is known as a:
questions.explanation: This form was perfected by Robert Browning.

questions.q: Tennyson's massive elegiac poem, 'In Memoriam', was written to mourn the death of:
questions.explanation: He wrote it for his close Cambridge friend, Arthur Henry Hallam (A.H.H.).

questions.q: Which poet wrote the chilling dramatic monologue 'My Last Duchess'?
questions.explanation: Browning is famous for this psychological portrait of a murderous Renaissance Duke.

questions.q: Which Brontë sister wrote the novel 'Wuthering Heights', featuring the brooding character Heathcliff?
questions.explanation: Emily Brontë wrote only one novel, the intensely passionate Wuthering Heights.

questions.q: Who wrote the famous lines ''Tis better to have loved and lost / Than never to have loved at all'?
questions.explanation: This famous quote is from Tennyson's 'In Memoriam A.H.H.'.

questions.q: The character of Bertha Mason, the 'madwoman in the attic', appears in which landmark Victorian novel?
questions.explanation: Bertha Mason is Mr. Rochester's hidden wife in Charlotte Brontë's 'Jane Eyre'.

questions.q: The publication of which scientific work in 1859 profoundly shook the religious faith of the Victorian literary world?
options: Darwin's On the Origin of Species
questions.explanation: Darwin's theory of evolution challenged literal interpretations of the Bible, causing deep anxiety.

questions.q: The line 'To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield' concludes which famous poem by Tennyson?
options: The Charge of the Light Brigade
questions.explanation: It is the concluding resolution of the aging hero in the dramatic monologue 'Ulysses'.
